exercises.title: A ring buffer
exercises.task: Read Ring: a fixed array, head where the next element leaves, count elements in use. The back wraps around to the start with %. Run traces the array as jobs come and go: the slots are reused, nothing is ever copied or reallocated.

exercises.title: Write Enqueue and Dequeue
exercises.task: Fill Enqueue (refuse when full) and Dequeue (refuse when empty). The only arithmetic is where the back is, and moving head with wrap-around.
hints: The back slot is head + count, wrapped: (r.head + r.count) % len(r.buf).
Dequeue takes r.buf[r.head], then moves head one step, wrapped the same way.
Without %, the indices run past the end of the array after the first lap.

exercises.title: Round-robin scheduling
exercises.task: A CPU (or a CI runner) shares its time between jobs: each job runs for at most quantum units, then goes to the back of the queue if it is not done. Return the names in the order the jobs finish.
hints: A slice works as a queue here: take q[0], then q = q[1:]; append unfinished jobs at the back.
A job that needs exactly quantum finishes in its turn: it does not go back in the queue.
